text:
kevin: Heads-up — I'm sketching a proposal for a new canary guard that looks at both relative deltas and absolute signals across slices (latency, errors, token throughput). Want feedback on the API shape and console UX before I wire it into rollout-service.

lisa: nice. do you mean a single guard rule that compares canary vs baseline, or one rule per metric? (eg p95 latency delta + error rate absolute)

kevin: single guard object that contains a list of metric checks. each check can be either 'delta' (canary vs baseline) or 'absolute' (threshold on canary). this keeps the UI compact and the service simple.

maria: +1 for the hybrid model. users constantly ask for both types. for alerts we should support a 'min-traffic' requirement so noisy low-volume slices don't fire. also we need to expose sample counts in the drilldown.

kevin: agreed. here's the rough guard JSON I was thinking of:

```
{
  "guard_name": "canary-safety-v2",
  "min_traffic": 1000,
  "checks": [
    {"metric":"p95_latency_ms","type":"delta","max_relative":1.15},
    {"metric":"error_rate","type":"absolute","max":0.02},
    {"metric":"token_throughput","type":"delta","min_relative":0.9}
  ],
  "window": "5m",
  "suppress_for": "10m"
}
```

lisa: looks good. nit: use clearer names (p95_latency_ms -> latency_p95) so frontend mapping is simpler. also we should include "direction" for metrics (higher-is-worse vs lower-is-worse) to avoid mistakes.

kevin: good point. I'll add direction and human-readable labels. also thinking of adding an optional "slice_weight_adjustment" to let canary slices with known skews be normalized.

sam: on the console side, proposal: in the rollout view show a compact 'guard pass' pill per guard (green/yellow/red). clicking opens a modal with a three-column drilldown: metric sparkline, canary vs baseline delta, sample table (top user segments). include a quick link to "promote" if all guards pass.

maria: +1. add a toggle to show raw counts vs rate-normalized numbers. important for embeddings and batching workloads.

kevin: question for eng-platform — do we want guards evaluated in the control plane or the serving plane? pros/cons?

lisa: control plane easier for cross-region aggregation and consistent baseline calculation. serving plane could be lower-latency for tiny windows but increases deployment surface.

sam: we already stream metrics to metrics-service; control plane evals can subscribe to a 'rollout.window' stream. we should keep evals colocated with metrics-service for less duplication.

kevin: sounds like control plane it is. ops-bot, can you create a telemetry ticket to add baseline joins + sample counts to the rollout stream?

ops-bot: Created ticket INF-4823: "rollout-stream: include baseline joins + sample counts" — https://redwood.internal/tickets/INF-4823 :white_check_mark:

maria: one more — alerting: should we create a single alert per guard or per failing check? ops tends to prefer one-per-guard with expanded details in payload.

lisa: agree, one-per-guard. payload should include failed_check_ids, metric snapshots, and sample hashes for quick investigation.

kevin: ok action items for me: (1) normalize guard JSON with direction + labels + slice min traffic, (2) add slice_weight_adjustment param, (3) PR for control-plane eval hookup. Sam: mockup the modal and pill states, Maria: write a short runbook snippet for oncall. I'll ping when PR is ready.

sam: I'll drop a Figma link by EOD and wire the promote button to the rollout API stub.

maria: will draft runbook. think we should also add a 're-run eval' button in case of transient spikes.

kevin: perfect. thanks team :pray:
